newsitem.title: FINLAND: BOREALIS SAYS MARKET FAVOURABLE SHORT-TERM.
newsitem.headline: BOREALIS SAYS MARKET FAVOURABLE SHORT-TERM.

text.p: Denmark based petrochemicals group Borealis A/S -- owned by Finland's Neste and Norway's Statoil -- said in a statement on Wednesday its market situation was favourable, but also sensitive.
"The short-term market situation is favourable, with stable polyolefins prices and falling feedstock prices," it said.
"Nevertheless, the European market outlook is highly sensitive to the strength of its overall economy and the global poloyolefins balance," it added.
The fundamentals of the polyolefins industry in 1997 would be affected by new capacity which is scheduled to come on stream during the next two years, Borealis said.

In 1996, Borealis' pretax profit fell to 870 million Danish crowns from 2.63 billion crowns in 1995. Polyolefin prices were at the start of 1996 but improved in the first half and were stable in the second, it said.
